rationale: The Save submit button is last in the DOM but carries tabindex="1", which forces it to the front of the tab sequence ahead of the name and bio inputs, breaking the field-then-submit order.
citation: "Failure of Success Criterion 2.4.3 due to using tabindex to create a tab order that does not preserve meaning and operability." — Failure F44

rationale: The Promotions nav link uses tabindex="99"; any value greater than 0 is positive, so it is hoisted ahead of every element without a positive tabindex, disrupting the Home/World/Promotions reading sequence.
citation: "If a Web page can be navigated sequentially and the navigation sequences affect meaning or operation, focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability." — WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A)

rationale: The mid-page "API reference" link sets tabindex="5", a positive value, pulling it ahead of the earlier "install the CLI" link and the later "deploy" link, so tab order no longer follows the documented step order.
citation: "Failure of Success Criterion 2.4.3 due to using tabindex to create a tab order that does not preserve meaning and operability." — Failure F44

rationale: The custom Stop control (role=button div) uses tabindex="2" while its siblings use tabindex="0"; the positive value reorders the player controls so Stop is reached before Play.
citation: "focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability." — WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A)

rationale: Question 3 is last in the DOM but tabindex="1" makes it the first element focused, jumping focus backward and forcing the user to complete the final question before the earlier ones.

rationale: Three checkout inputs carry tabindex 3, 1, 2 respectively; the competing positive values make Tab visit Expiry then CVC then Card number, scrambling the natural card-entry order.

citation: "Failure of Success Criterion 2.4.3 due to using tabindex to create a tab order that does not preserve meaning and operability." — Failure F44

rationale: The Subscribe button uses tabindex="01", which under HTML integer parsing is the positive value 1; it reorders focus ahead of the email input. A naive string match for "1" would miss it, but the value is genuinely positive so the runner should flag it.
citation: "Failure of Success Criterion 2.4.3 due to using tabindex to create a tab order that does not preserve meaning and operability." — Failure F44

rationale: Every toolbar control uses tabindex="0"; none is positive, so the tab order matches DOM order (Bold, Italic, Underline). F44 only triggers on values greater than 0, so this passes.
citation: "Failure of Success Criterion 2.4.3 due to using tabindex to create a tab order that does not preserve meaning and operability." — Failure F44

rationale: The status region uses tabindex="-1" so script can focus it; a negative value keeps it out of the Tab sequence entirely and cannot reorder anything, so F44 does not apply.

rationale: The registration form uses only native inputs and a submit button with no tabindex attributes, so focus follows native DOM order and no positive tabindex exists to violate F44.

rationale: The custom slider is made keyboard-focusable with tabindex="0", the correct technique; zero is not a positive value, so it sits in DOM order and does not trigger F44.
citation: "Failure of Success Criterion 2.4.3 due to using tabindex to create a tab order that does not preserve meaning and operability." — Failure F44

rationale: The skip link is a plain anchor with no tabindex; it is first in the DOM and first in the tab order, which preserves meaning and operability. No positive tabindex is present.

rationale: The route heading uses tabindex="-1" so the SPA can move focus to it on navigation; the negative value keeps it out of the Tab sequence, so it cannot reorder focus and F44 is not triggered.

rationale: The shipping form mixes native input, select, and button elements with no tabindex attributes, so the tab order follows DOM order and there is no positive tabindex to violate F44.

rationale: The Apply button is visually moved to the front via CSS order:-1, but no positive tabindex is set, so the actual tab order remains DOM order. rationale: The live-chat link explicitly sets tabindex="0", which is redundant on a native anchor but not a positive value; the link stays in DOM order and F44 is not triggered.

rationale: The page's only focusable control carries tabindex="2" — the deterministic positive-tabindex pattern fires — but with a single focusable element there is no other component whose order could be disrupted, so whether meaning/operability is actually broken is genuinely ambiguous; the runner may reasonably abstain rather than assert a defect.
